newsitem.title: USA: No sign of U.S. inflation -- White House's Munnell.
newsitem.headline: No sign of U.S. inflation -- White House's Munnell.

text.p: White House economist Alicia Munnell said on Tuesday that she saw no signs of inflation or even precursors of inflation pressure in the U.S. economy.
"Inflationary pressures take time to build," Munnell told Reuters Financial Television.

"We don't see even the precursors of inflation, so we don't see inflationary wage pressures, we don't see real botlenecks in the economy, we don't see any of the things that would tell you, 'heads up, be careful, you're going to see inflation down the road,'" she added.
But Munnell noted that the May unemployment rate of 4.8 percent was probably near the low end of estimates of the non-accelerating inflation rate of unemployment, or NAIRU.
"I think 4.8 is probably at the low end of that (NAIRU) band and the economy is pushing to see how far it can go without creating inflationary pressures and so far, so good," Munnell said.
Munnell declined to estimate the economy's growth pace in the second quarter, but acknowledged it appeared to have slowed from the 5.8 percent growth in gross domestic product in the first quarter.
"I'm glad it's slowing down from 5.8 percent in the first quarter. That was not a sustainable pace," Munnell added.
